data.notes: Overland Plaza is a 205,918 SF grocery-anchored community center in Overland, MO that recently completed a $21M comprehensive redevelopment, resulting in new construction, refreshed facades, roof replacements, and new HVAC throughout. The asset is 100% leased to a 22-year average-tenure roster of national tenants anchored by the dominant St. Louis grocer Schnucks (37-year tenure, 68,195 SF), with Ross, Marshalls, Five Below, Dollar Tree, and McDonald's as co-anchors. While the near-term rollover profile is favorable (only 3.97% of revenue through Year 2), investors should carefully underwrite the material 2030 rollover (38% of GLA, including Schnucks at below-market $8.00/SF) and the fixed CID RE tax structure that governs property taxes through 2048.

redFlags.description: Barnes & Noble (19.5% of GLA, 21,875 SF) expires January 2021 with NO renewal options and consistently declining sales ($219.79/SF in 2012 to $193.77/SF in 2015). Given secular decline of brick-and-mortar bookstores, re-leasing risk is substantial and 9-month downtime assumption may be optimistic.

Lease expiration concentration: 94.2% of GLA expires between February 2019 and January 2021, including the anchor (62.68% of GLA) in May 2020. While Stop & Shop has renewal options, the execution of renewals across virtually all tenants within a 2-year window creates meaningful rollover and re-leasing risk.
Hallmark (6,575 SF inline) has no renewal options, declining sales trend, and lease expires Feb 2019. Re-leasing inline space at $26/SF market rent in Glastonbury, CT carries execution risk.

FedEx Office co-tenancy/termination clause: if Stop & Shop or Barnes & Noble assigns their lease to a competing retailer, FedEx Office may terminate — creating potential income disruption linked to the two largest tenants' lease actions.

data.notes: The Commons is a 279,201 SF dual grocery-anchored power center in Martinsburg, WV — a rapidly growing D.C. exurban market — offering 99.6% occupancy, a Year 1 NOI of $4.5M, a 10-year NOI CAGR of 2.41%, and meaningful mark-to-market upside on ±46K SF of below-market leases expiring in the hold. The asset benefits from market-dominant positioning with limited competition, an investment-grade anchor lineup averaging 14.6 years of operating tenure, strong tenant sales metrics (11.1% portfolio health ratio), and favorable Berkeley County demographic tailwinds including 11.1% population growth since 2020. Key risks include a near-term WALT of only 3.73 years requiring active re-leasing of ±74% of GLA by FY2030, aging 2008 TPO roofs covering the majority of the center's square footage approaching end of useful life, and elevated occupancy costs for Books-A-Million (25.1%) and The Vape Saloon (38.4%) signaling potential rollover risk.

data.notes: University Hills is a 209,956 SF grocery-anchored community center in Denver's Central submarket, 100% occupied and anchored by a new 20-year King Soopers lease (Kroger, BBB-rated) at $10.50 PSF with $70MM in annual sales, supported by a strong national co-tenancy including Marshalls, Michael's, PetSmart, and Ulta Beauty. The $56.5M purchase price is being financed with a $33.9M loan (60% LTPP) at 5.50%, with Kroger contributing $4.5MM of equity at close, generating Year 1 NOI after reserves of $3.60M, a 1.56x amortizing DSCR, and 10.6% debt yield. Key risks include significant near-term lease rollover (~35% of non-anchor GLA expiring within 12 months) and pervasive co-tenancy clauses that could trigger rent reductions across multiple tenants if anchor traffic or occupancy declines.

redFlags.description: Five leases expire within 12 months of projected closing (Michael's Feb-25, PetSmart Jan-25, Office Depot Sep-25, America's Best Contacts Oct-25, Great Clips Nov-25), representing approximately 74,210 SF or ~35% of non-anchor GLA, creating near-term rollover and re-leasing execution risk.

data.notes: Knightdale Marketplace is a 323,113 SF, 100%-occupied super-regional power center in the fastest-growing submarket of the Raleigh MSA, featuring a high-performing lineup of national retailers led by TJ Maxx ($585 PSF sales), Saltgrass ($1,230 PSF), and Qdoba ($949 PSF), with ~$110,000 SF of leases executed in the last two years (HomeGoods, Burlington, Academy Sports, Barnes & Noble) significantly upgrading the merchandising mix. The property offers a compelling combination of durable income (6.6-year WALT, 2.4% 10-year NOI CAGR from $5.86M to $7.44M), ~$1.5M of mark-to-market rent upside on ~55% of below-market GLA, and strong demographic tailwinds from explosive residential development, the I-540 expansion, and proximity to major employers including Novo Nordisk's $4.1B expansion. Key risks include original-age roofs on multiple major boxes, TJ Maxx lease expiry in 2028, near-term outparcel expirations (Arby's, Saltgrass), and co-tenancy dependencies on NAP shadow anchors (Target, Home Depot) that are not part of the sale.

redFlags.description: Multiple original-age roofs (likely ~18 years old, installed 2007/2008) on major anchor boxes including TJ Maxx (26,297 SF), Best Buy (30,000 SF), and smaller suites (C1-C3, D1-D3, Building 11) with no warranty or installation year data, plus expired warranties on Ross Dress for Less (2006, 30,144 SF) and Outbuilding 200 (2008). Combined at-risk roof area exceeds 100,000 SF and represents a potentially material near-term capital expenditure.

TJ Maxx lease expires October 2028 (~2.5 years remaining) with only two 5-year options at modest rents ($11.10/$11.60 PSF). This is the center's highest-volume tenant ($15.4MM sales / $585 PSF) and triggers co-tenancy remedies for Burlington Coat Factory; non-renewal would be a significant credit and income event.

Two outparcel ground leases (Arby's expiring Dec-2026 and Saltgrass expiring Jan-2027) are at or within 6-12 months of expiration at analysis start date (Aug 2026), creating near-term rollover risk totaling ~$344,000 of annual base rent.

Kirkland's (6,240 SF, $139,230 annual rent) has no renewal options remaining and expires July 2027; the brand has faced significant financial distress and store closure history, raising concern about whether the tenant will exercise its space beyond the analysis assumption of rolling to market.

Multiple major tenants have co-tenancy provisions tied to Target and/or Home Depot (both NAP parcels not included in the sale), meaning the seller/future owner has no control over these critical co-tenancy anchors; a Target or Home Depot closure would trigger reduced rent or termination rights for Rainbow, Rainbow, Arby's, GNC, Visionworks, Rack Room Shoes, Michaels, PetSmart and others.

Barnes & Noble is a new entrant to this submarket with no established sales history at this location; while the lease is executed and buildout is active, it serves as a key co-tenancy anchor for PetSmart and Ross, adding execution risk in the near term.

data.notes: Westwood Town Center is a 226,155 SF Home Depot and Marc's-anchored community shopping center in affluent Rocky River, OH (Cleveland MSA) built in 1988, featuring 30-year average tenant tenure, 95% occupancy, and a Year 1 NOI of $2.34M growing to $2.64M at stabilization (4.7% CAGR). The deal offers genuine value-add through 10,650 SF of vacancy, below-market anchor and shop rents, and a potential outlot development, though investors must underwrite near-term anchor lease expirations (Marc's Nov-2029, AMC Feb-2029), cascading co-tenancy risk, and a material LL-responsibility roof replacement requirement across approximately 55,000+ SF rated 4 or below with 3-7 years remaining life. The Cleveland suburban retail market provides strong fundamental support with record-low availability and rising asking rents, making this a compelling but execution-dependent opportunity for a buyer able to manage anchor rollover and capital needs.

data.notes: Markland Plaza is a 172,475 SF grocery-anchored shopping center in Kokomo, Indiana, anchored by Best Buy, Burlington, ALDI, PetSmart, Ross Dress for Less, and Five Below, offered free and clear at 96.5% occupancy with in-place NOI of $2,207,105 and a 5-year NOI CAGR of 3.58%. The center benefits from a market-dominant position at the primary retail intersection in north central Indiana, significant near-term economic tailwinds from $5.7B in EV gigafactory investment, and long-term stability from ALDI's 20-year lease with seven 5-year options, though investors must underwrite a concentrated 2028-2029 anchor rollover affecting ~60% of GLA and deeply below-market ALDI rent. The recent subdivision of the ALDI and power center parcels creates optionality for the buyer to generate arbitrage value by selling stabilized components independently.

ALDI rent is deeply below market at $4.70 PSF on 22,245 SF (12.9% of GLA) versus $15.00 NNN market; no meaningful mark-to-market until 2028/2033 bumps, significantly compressing NOI and limiting upside from the grocery anchor.

Best Buy (NYSE: BBY) secular headwind: consumer electronics big-box retail is under ongoing pressure from e-commerce; 29,957 SF is the largest tenant by SF and 16.18% of revenue, with one remaining 5-year option upon 2029 expiry — replacement risk would be material.

Original 1974 buildings have no disclosed roof replacement history; if roofs are near or beyond useful life, significant unbudgeted capital expenditures could arise. The OM only discloses roof replacement dates for 2018 and 2019 construction — the 1974 vintage structures (containing Burlington and Best Buy inline space) are not addressed beyond the Burlington/Best Buy roof replaced in 2019.

Skechers (8,000 SF) lease has a sales kickout clause after year 5 if trailing 12-month sales are below $1.5M; the analysis assumes lease execution and excludes $459,105 in associated costs, overstating near-term NOI if the kickout is exercised.

Two near-term lease expirations in 2025-2026: Centennial Wireless (3,750 SF, Nov-2025) and Xfinity (4,035 SF, Jan-2026) represent ~4.5% of GLA with unresolved renewal status, adding short-term leasing uncertainty.

data.notes:
Markland Mall is a 309,237 SF regional mall in Kokomo, Indiana offering monopolistic trade area positioning as the only enclosed mall within ~50 miles, supported by two owned anchor tenants (Target and Dunham's Sports) on active leases and strong in-line sales performance with a 9.41% average occupancy cost. The investment thesis centers on Kokomo's $5.7B EV gigafactory-driven economic boom, value-add lease-up of 5,990 SF of vacancy and specialty re-leasing, and projected NOI growth from $2.9M to $4.3M through 2030 at an 8.63% CAGR. Key risks include a severe 2025-2028 lease rollover wave encompassing 67.5% of GLA (including the critical Target anchor at $1.70 PSF expiring Jan-2028), small-market exit liquidity constraints, and several tenants with stressed occupancy cost ratios requiring active asset management.

Markland Plaza is a 172,475 SF grocery-anchored shopping center in Kokomo, Indiana, anchored by Best Buy, Burlington, ALDI, PetSmart, Ross Dress for Less, and Five Below, offered free and clear at 96.5% occupancy with in-place NOI of $2,207,105 and a 5-year NOI CAGR of 3.58%. The center benefits from a market-dominant position at the primary retail intersection in north central Indiana, significant near-term economic tailwinds from $5.7B in EV gigafactory investment, and long-term stability from ALDI's 20-year lease with seven 5-year options, though investors must underwrite a concentrated 2028-2029 anchor rollover affecting ~60% of GLA and deeply below-market ALDI rent. The recent subdivision of the ALDI and power center parcels creates optionality for the buyer to generate arbitrage value by selling stabilized components independently.

redFlags.description: Target (107,559 SF, 34.78% of GLA) lease expires January 2028 at only $1.70 PSF — loss of this anchor would be catastrophic for mall viability and represents the single largest near-term risk to the investment thesis.
Massive rollover concentration: 67.49% of total SF (209,090 SF) expires through 2028, requiring successful re-leasing across dozens of tenants in a small Midwestern market to achieve projected NOI.
Serenity Spa and Boutique (Suite 0D09A) has a 53.90% occupancy cost ratio — at $78 PSF sales, this tenant is deeply underwater and at significant risk of closure or default.

Gravity 765 (17,999 SF entertainment tenant) has a 27.47% occupancy cost at $37/SF sales; analysis assumes renewal at same below-market $10.25 PSF rather than exercising its option, indicating weak performance and negotiating leverage.

Main mall roof installed 2011 is approximately 13 years old; with a typical TPO lifespan of 20-30 years, a significant capital expenditure for roof replacement may be required within the hold period, particularly given the large mall footprint.

FYE (3,990 SF) and Hibbett Sporting Goods (5,412 SF) pay $0 base rent with only percentage rent; FYE faces secular pressure from physical media decline and Hibbett faces competition from larger sporting goods retailers.

Multiple specialty tenants (6 suites) have below-market leases with near-term 2025 expirations, though OM assumes continuation and market re-leasing upside of ~$595,653 in potential incremental revenue.

Concentrated near-term rollover risk: Best Buy (29,957 SF, Jan-2029), PetSmart (19,392 SF, Sep-2028), Ross (18,000 SF, Jan-2029), Carter's (5,139 SF, Jan-2029), and AT&T (4,050 SF, Jan-2029) all expire within approximately 4 years, representing ~44% of GLA rolling in a 12-month window and creating significant re-leasing execution risk.

ALDI rent is deeply below market at $4.70 PSF on 22,245 SF (12.9% of GLA) versus $15.00 NNN market; no meaningful mark-to-market until 2028/2033 bumps, significantly compressing NOI and limiting upside from the grocery anchor.

Best Buy (NYSE: BBY) secular headwind: consumer electronics big-box retail is under ongoing pressure from e-commerce; 29,957 SF is the largest tenant by SF and 16.18% of revenue, with one remaining 5-year option upon 2029 expiry — replacement risk would be material.

Original 1974 buildings have no disclosed roof replacement history; if roofs are near or beyond useful life, significant unbudgeted capital expenditures could arise. The OM only discloses roof replacement dates for 2018 and 2019 construction — the 1974 vintage structures (containing Burlington and Best Buy inline space) are not addressed beyond the Burlington/Best Buy roof replaced in 2019.

Skechers (8,000 SF) lease has a sales kickout clause after year 5 if trailing 12-month sales are below $1.5M; the analysis assumes lease execution and excludes $459,105 in associated costs, overstating near-term NOI if the kickout is exercised.

Two near-term lease expirations in 2025-2026: Centennial Wireless (3,750 SF, Nov-2025) and Xfinity (4,035 SF, Jan-2026) represent ~4.5% of GLA with unresolved renewal status, adding short-term leasing uncertainty.

data.notes: Damascus Shopping Center is a 143,631 SF grocery-anchored community center in Damascus, MD anchored by an outperforming Safeway ($582/SF in 2025 sales, 84th percentile nationally for visits) in the affluent, supply-constrained northern tip of Montgomery County with $199K average household income in a 5-mile radius. The deal offers a compelling value-add story – Year 1 NOI of $2.476M growing at a 5.7% CAGR over 5 years – through lease-up of 19,583 SF of vacancy and marking 29,571 SF of below-market legacy rents to market for a combined $705K+ of incremental revenue potential. Key risks include near-term lease rollover concentration in Years 1-3, a landlord TI obligation to Safeway of up to $875K, two aging roof sections due for replacement by 2028, and the structural dependency of multiple co-tenancy clauses on Safeway's continued operation.

redFlags.description: Sections A and C of the landlord-responsible roof (EPDM, installed 2008, combined ~29,100 SF) are approaching their 2028 warranty expiration at approximately 17 years of age, indicating likely near-term roof replacement capital expenditure.

Damascus Studio of Dance operates as a dance studio, which is an explicitly prohibited use under Safeway's lease. The landlord does not have a copy of a Safeway waiver on file, creating potential lease compliance risk with the anchor tenant.

Safeway (38% of rental revenue) carries a Non-Investment Grade credit rating (BB+/Ba2 as Albertsons subsidiary) with co-tenancy clauses in Dollar Tree and Chipotle leases that could trigger rent reductions to 50% and 75% respectively, and ultimately lease terminations, if Safeway goes dark.
Landlord has an outstanding TI obligation to Safeway of up to $875,370 due by September 10, 2027, representing a near-term capital commitment that prospective buyers must underwrite.

Multiple near-term lease expirations within 18 months of analysis start (Advance Auto Parts Nov-27, Dollar Tree Mar-28, T-Mobile Nov-27, New Smiles Kids Dentistry Dec-27, Damascus Studio of Dance Jun-27, Mathnasium Nov-26 vacating) create meaningful rollover risk and re-leasing costs concentrated in Years 1-3.

dealScore.rationale: High-performing grocery-anchored center with a dominant Safeway (8+ years term, top-quartile sales) in an affluent, supply-constrained Montgomery County submarket, offset by meaningful near-term lease rollover, elevated Year 1 vacancy (14%), and several legacy tenants with below-market rents requiring lease-up capital.
strengths: Safeway anchor with $33.9M in 2025 sales ($582/SF), 4.0% health ratio, 4.6% YOY sales growth, and 8.2 years of remaining term with 7x5 renewal options
Located in Montgomery County – one of the nation's wealthiest counties – with $199K avg HHI in 5-mile radius and $3.2B buying power
Market-dominant center with 2.4M annual visits (84th percentile among neighborhood centers nationally) and only 15 retail SF per capita within 5 miles (38% below national average)
77% of GLA and 71% of rental revenue derived from national tenants with strong average tenure of 14.2 years
Two investment-grade pad sites (McDonald's ground lease, Dunkin'/Baskin Robbins) with spin-off potential
5-year NOI CAGR of 5.7% with clear lease-up path adding $525,722 of incremental rental revenue
Strong mark-to-market opportunity: $179,630 of incremental revenue from below-market legacy tenants (30% below market on average)
Supply-constrained submarket with no development pipeline and Damascus High School undergoing $127M renovation expanding capacity
